title: Product Photo Compression: Faster Pages Without Obvious Quality Loss
description: Compress product photos for faster pages while protecting visible quality, transparency, and marketplace requirements.

blocks.text: If your product page takes more than a short processing step to load, you've already lost half your buyers. Google knows this—and ranks fast sites higher.
The #1 culprit? Bloated product images. Here's how to fix it.
Why Compression Matters
Every second of load time costs:

items.text: Bounce rate (visitors leave before seeing product)

blocks.text: Your beautifully edited photos are worthless if they take 4 seconds to load.
The Right Compression Target
Rule of thumb: Product images should be under 200KB each on your storefront. Under 500KB max.
If your files are 2-5MB, you're bleeding conversions.
The Compression Workflow
Step 1: Edit at high resolution (edit-photo.com works at native resolution).
Step 2: Export at appropriate final dimensions:
Step 3: Compress with quality 80-85% (JPEG) or use WebP.
Step 4: Test load speed on mobile.
Format Selection Guide

items.text: JPEG: Best for photos with lots of colors, no transparency
PNG: Best when transparency matters, but larger files
WebP: Best overall (25-35% smaller than JPEG at same quality)

blocks.text: Most modern platforms support WebP. Shopify auto-converts on upload.
The Transparent PNG Trap
Transparent PNGs from edit-photo.com are perfect for compositing—but they're heavy files.
Rule: Keep transparent PNGs as your master files. Export final versions as JPEG or WebP with backgrounds baked in.
Mobile-First Reality
80%+ of e-commerce traffic is mobile. Your photos must load fast on 4G/5G, not just your WiFi.
Test on your phone with WiFi off. If images take more than 2 seconds to appear, they're too heavy.
The Bulk Compression Approach
For catalogs of a larger catalog:

items.text: Run through a bulk compressor (TinyPNG, Squoosh)

blocks.text: Two hours of work. Massive Core Web Vitals improvement.
The Alt Text Bonus
While you're optimizing images, add proper alt text to every one. Google reads alt text for:
Match alt text to your target keyword naturally. Don't stuff.
The Compound Effect
Fast, compressed, well-edited product photos + descriptive filenames + strong alt text = a compound SEO win most sellers ignore.
Compare two identical products:

items.text: Seller A: 4MB unoptimized photos, generic filenames, no alt text
Seller B: 200KB WebP photos, descriptive filenames, keyword-rich alt text

blocks.text: Seller B outranks Seller A. Every time.
Start Optimizing
